messages:
marta: heads-up — saw two customer incidents where short-lived runtime overrides vanished after a subsequent config publish. looks like the console writes an override without persistent provenance so the api merge wins and nukes the override :/
kevin: ugh. do we have an example sequence? is this the ttl-based overrides or manual user toggles? :thinking_face:
samir: sequence from prod: user sets override via console (tenant A), later patch via automated job (owner: config-migrator) publishes same key -> override gone. override had TTL 1h.
marta: exact. console creates override with {source: "console", op_id: "u-123", ttl: 3600, value: {...}}; publish is standard patch with last_write_wins.
olivia: naive LWW is the issue. we need some kind of lightweight reconciliation so temporary overrides are either preserved or surfaced for manual re-apply.
tia: options: 1) server-side merge rule (preserve any active override if newer than publish), 2) add immutable override ledger (append-only events), 3) include override metadata in the config doc (owner/op_id/ttl) and teach API to respect it.
kevin: 3 seems simplest API-change wise: add override metadata fields in the canonical config schema. but that's a schema bump — we'd need migration and console + sdk changes.
amy: from UX POV we want to show "active overrides" per key and who set them, plus a quick reapply button if the system detects a conflicting publish. lightweight ledger would let us surface diffs in the console timeline.
rollouts-bot: note: proposal will affect telemetry volume; track event cardinality if we append every override op.
samir: agree on telemetry cost. suggestion: keep append-only ledger but sample high-volume tenants and store full events for admin queries. for others store summarized latest active override + sampled history.
kevin: API contract idea: when creating an override, server returns op_id + etag and stores override as a distinct object: /v1/tenants/:id/overrides/:op_id. publish pipeline checks active overrides and either (a) marks conflict and returns 409 with list of active op_ids, or (b) auto-merge if flag allow_auto_merge=true.
marta: example payload for override create: ```json
{
  "key": "routing.max_qps",
  "value": 200,
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "created_by": "marta",
  "source": "console"
}
```
olivia: on conflict response 409 we should include minimal resolver hints: current_override_metadata (op_id, expires_at, created_by) and a boolean resolved_by_auto_merge. console can then surface a banner: "Publish conflicts with active override: reapply / keep / cancel".
tia: SRE question — what's the perf hit for checking overrides on every publish? current publish path is hot.
kevin: keep it fast: overrides live in a small redis shard keyed by tenant+key. publish reads TTL and created_at only; no heavy reads. only when user clicks "view history" do we fetch full append events from blob store.
rollouts-bot: telemetry: emit override.create, override.expire, override.conflict events with sampling rules. include op_id and tenant_id. sample by tenant bucket to avoid skew.
amy: UI: two small changes — a per-key inline pill showing active override and a timeline drawer that fetches sampled history. reapply action makes a new override op (not mutating older op).
samir: migration plan: 1) add override endpoints and telemetry (beta), 2) console integration behind a flag, 3) roll out sampling rules and cleanup job for expired ops, 4) deprecate in-place override fields after 90 days.
marta: approvals? need eng-platform owner + eng-sre + console-design. also request product buy-in since UX will expose more noisy info to users.
kevin: i'll draft the API PR. can someone from eng-sre review perf implications? @samir?
samir: on it. i'll run a perf simulation (publish qps) and post numbers here tomorrow.
olivia: i'll sketch the banner copy and timeline microcopy, will ping amy for design review.
amy: happy to review — prefer small incremental UI, keep default collapsed. :+1:
kevin: thanks. i'll drop a short RFC in #eng-platform-docs and tag reviewers.
marta: thanks team. follow-ups: add issue in backlog, assign owners, and we should include a brief e2e test for the race scenario. :eyes:
